name: The Charlatans
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Rob Collins's Hammond organ made the Charlatans, and his death in 1996, halfway through their biggest record, should have ended them. They finished it with a borrowed keyboard player and went to number one.

hero.by: Photo: Edwardrhodes06 (Scarborough Open Air Theatre, June 2024)

eras.title: The Spencer Davis Group on E
eras.text: Bassist Martin Blunt built the band around Rob Collins's Hammond organ and Jon Brookes's drums, West Midlands soul and R&B with acid house leaking in. They had a manager with a record shop and a window to put a sign in. They needed a singer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Some Friendly · Wikipedia: The Charlatans
years.h: Martin Blunt starts again after Makin' Time
years.p: Blunt, singer-guitarist Baz Ketley and drummer Jon Brookes jam their way into a band. [[Rob Collins|bfaa8d8e-51eb-4f6c-ad28-c2ad13dbfa52]], who'd played with Brookes as a teenager, takes the organ.
years.xp:
They went through several keyboard players first. One of them died after four or five rehearsals, according to the Some Friendly history on Wikipedia.

Steve Harrison, who owned the Omega Music record shop and knew Blunt from Makin' Time, saw a set and agreed to manage them.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Charlatans · Wikipedia: Some Friendly
years.h: Support to [[The Stone Roses|b5fa29f1-6c22-4321-a488-b5f363b06b06]] at the London School of Economics
years.p: One of their earliest known gigs. Brookes said later they envied the confidence of Ian Brown and wished they had a singer like him.

years.h: Tim Burgess auditions in Walsall and gets told to stop doing an impression
years.p: Martin Blunt, after Burgess opened with his best Jim Morrison. Burgess, a Northwich lad from the Electric Crayons, was in by August; guitarist Jon Baker joined that July.
years.xp:
Harrison had put a 'vocalist required' sign in the Omega Music window. Burgess told the Guardian he'd once jumped on stage at a Charlatans gig and sung one of their songs; then came the call to come and hang out in the Midlands. The Electric Crayons' first single came out the day he joined.

Wikipedia's history of Some Friendly has the impression as Iggy Pop rather than Morrison. Ketley left after his girlfriend left him, by one account; Harrison said Ketley felt the band were going nowhere.

eras.title: "The only song they know"
eras.text: The band moved to Northwich, Burgess's and Harrison's hometown, and a song Burgess hummed on the way to buy cigarettes put them in the Top 10. Beggars Banquet's Situation Two imprint had a number one album inside a year.

years.cap: The Charlatans at the Joiners, Southampton, February 1990
yt: Live at the Ritz, Manchester, June 1990
years.h: 'Indian Rope' is an indie hit, and Situation Two signs them
years.p: Martin Mills of Beggars called them the most obviously commercial band the label had signed by then, and big from day one.

years.h: 'The Only One I Know' goes Top 10
years.p: Burgess got the tune walking to the garage for cigarettes, ran back to his parents' house for his Dictaphone, and never got the cigarettes.
years.xp:
They went to the Windings in Wrexham to record 'Polar Bear'. A friend, Jonah, told them they were recording the wrong song, and a fax from Beggars said the same. Blunt told Jon Baker to make his guitar line "sound like morse code"; Burgess was stuck in a tailback on the M6 and added his vocal later.

Chris Nagle mixed it at Strawberry in Stockport, where he'd worked with Martin Hannett on Joy Division. Blunt says they turned down Top of the Pops like the Clash had and still went Top 10; Wikipedia's Some Friendly article says the single earned their first TOTP appearance.

years.h: Some Friendly enters at number one
years.p: Situation Two, produced by Chris Nagle. The BPI certified it gold three days after release, though plenty of critics heard the influences more than the band.

years.cap: Tim Burgess at the Joiners, Southampton, February 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: The Charlatans · Wikipedia: Some Friendly
years.h: In America they become the Charlatans UK
years.p: A 1960s San Francisco band already owned the name in the US, so the Charlatans append 'UK' for their first American shows.

years.cap: Flyer for Dave Haslam's Freedom night at the Boardwalk, Manchester, with the Charlatans on the bill, January 1, 1991
years.h: Jon Baker leaves after 'Over Rising'; Mark Collins arrives
years.p: The new guitarist is no relation to Rob Collins.

years.h: Flood produces, and the title is a New York address
years.p: Between 10th and 11th is where the Marquee stood, site of their first US gig. The album missed the Top 20; 'Weirdo' made it.
years.xp: To stay in view they ran the Daytripper weekends in Blackpool and Brighton with [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Rob Collins · Wikipedia: The Charlatans
years.h: Rob Collins is charged with armed robbery
years.p: A friend robbed an off-licence while Collins waited in the car. Collins pleaded guilty to assisting an offender, got eight months and served four.
years.xp: Collins said he knew nothing of the robbery until he heard a gunshot from inside the shop and saw his friend come out. He later admitted he shouldn't have picked him up once he realised what had happened. The armed robbery charge was dropped in court; he was released in early 1994.

eras.title: Back at the top, through Rockfield
eras.text: With Collins back, the band hit number one again, then went to Monmouthshire to make the record that became their biggest. Collins died partway through. They finished it with Primal Scream's keyboard player and played Knebworth weeks later.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Charlatans · Wikipedia: Tellin' Stories
years.h: Up to Our Hips reaches number 8
years.p: Collins is out of prison by early 1994. The album's 'Patrol' gets a remix from [[The Chemical Brothers|1946a82a-f927-40c2-8235-38d64f50d043]], who end up working on the next record too.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tellin' Stories · Wikipedia: The Charlatans
years.h: The self-titled fourth album goes to number one
years.p: 'Just When You're Thinkin' Things Over' reaches 12. The tour runs through America, Europe and two UK legs into 1996.
play: Just When You're Thinkin' Things Over

years.h: Two weeks in a Windermere cottage with Dylan and Wu-Tang
years.p: Burgess and Mark Collins write with an acoustic, a drum machine, an eight-track and a stack of records. Burgess studied how Dylan and Wu-Tang Clan used vocal rhythm.

years.h: At Monnow Valley, Rob Collins works the night shift
years.p: Burgess on what happened to daytime tracks once Collins and his own engineer, Ric Peet, got hold of them. After one argument Burgess told Mark Collins he wanted Rob out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tellin' Stories · Wikipedia: Rob Collins
years.h: Rob Collins is killed on the road from the pub to Rockfield
years.p: Driving his BMW on the B4233 near Monmouth, Collins hit a kerb and rolled through a hedge. He wasn't wearing a seatbelt; the coroner found more than double the legal alcohol level.
years.xp:
He was thrown from the car and stood up before collapsing; Wikipedia's Tellin' Stories article says he died in the ambulance to Abergavenny. Ric Peet, his passenger, had minor injuries. Mark Collins, driving ahead, had seen the headlights behind him disappear.

Collins's father urged the band to carry on. They cancelled a Loch Lomond date; Melody Maker ran tributes from Noel Gallagher, Mani, the Chemical Brothers and Black Grape's Wags.

years.cap: Ticket for Oasis at Knebworth Park, August 11, 1996, the day the Charlatans played
years.src: Wikipedia: Tellin' Stories · Wikipedia: The Charlatans
years.h: Nineteen days later, Knebworth with Oasis
years.p: Primal Scream were on a break, so Bobby Gillespie suggested [[Martin Duffy|00d21293-62c1-4c43-a394-b8fd9fa49853]]. He plays the two Oasis support shows and stays to help finish the album.

years.h: 'One to Another' comes out with clocks and dinosaurs on it
years.p: Tom Rowlands of the Chemical Brothers added those sounds and multi-tracked Rob Collins's piano. It reaches number three in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tellin' Stories · Wikipedia: The Charlatans
years.h: Tony Rogers takes the keyboard job for the UK tour
years.p: He becomes a permanent member and is still there.

years.h: Tellin' Stories goes to number one and platinum
years.p: Collins and Duffy are both on it, uncredited track by track out of respect for Collins. 'North Country Boy' is Burgess rewriting Dylan's 'Girl from the North Country' from the man's side.
years.xp: Q later put it among the 100 best albums of the 1990s. During a 2020 listening party Burgess and Mark Collins finally revealed Duffy's tracks: 'With No Shoes', 'Tellin' Stories', 'You're a Big Girl Now' and 'Get On It'.

eras.title: New labels, and a hole in the accounts
eras.text: With the Beggars contract done, the band moved to Universal, then Sanctuary, then gave an album away through a radio station. Along the way a court found that their accountant had been stealing from them since 1994.

years.h: The Beggars contract ends; the friendship doesn't
years.p: After the Melting Pot compilation they sign to Universal, but still help Beggars compile the B-sides set Songs From the Other Side and the Just Lookin' DVD.

years.h: Their accountant goes to prison for stealing £294,000
years.p: Trevor Williams told the band he was setting money aside for future tax bills. Chester Crown Court gave him five-year terms, to run together.
years.xp: Williams, 54 and unqualified, ran Trevor Williams Accounting Services in Middlewich. He stole from the Charlatans over four years from 1994, plus about £70,000 from two other clients, to keep his firm afloat. The judge called it "a breach of trust on a tremendous scale." None of the money was returned.

years.h: Us and Us Only turns a little country
years.p: The first Universal album and Tony Rogers's first on record. Burgess's love of Bob Dylan pulls the sound toward country.

years.cap: The Charlatans at the Hammersmith Apollo, London
years.h: Simpatico tries reggae and dub
years.p: Their first for Sanctuary, produced by Jim Lowe. It went Top 10 in its first week and dropped out of the chart soon after.

years.h: Opening for the Who and the Rolling Stones at Wembley
years.p: Both bands take them to Wembley and Twickenham stadiums. They also play Delamere Forest in Cheshire and sell the recording as a five-part download.

years.h: XFM gives away You Cross My Path
years.p: The Charlatans become the first UK band to release an album as a free download through a radio station. Cooking Vinyl puts out the CD and LP on May 19, 2008.

eras.title: Philadelphia, and a drummer lost
eras.text: Jon Brookes collapsed on stage in 2010 and was treated for a brain tumour for three years, still writing with the band. After he died they made two albums with borrowed drummers from the Verve, New Order and Factory Floor.

years.h: Jon Brookes collapses on stage in Philadelphia
years.p: He had a seizure mid-show and was diagnosed with a brain tumour. The Verve's Peter Salisbury drums the UK dates; Brookes is back for Christmas and New Year's Eve.
years.xp: Earlier that year the band played Some Friendly in full at Primavera Sound for its 20th anniversary. Who We Touch came out on September 6 and reached 21.

years.cap: Kevin Shields sits in at the Union Chapel, London, March 16, 2011
years.h: Kevin Shields joins the acoustic show at the Union Chapel
years.p: Burgess and Mark Collins tour the UK stripped down and release the Warm Sounds EP. [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]]'s Kevin Shields sits in at the London date.

years.h: Jon Brookes dies at 44
years.p: He had been treated for the brain tumour since 2010 and was writing new material with the band that summer. "We are torn apart," Burgess wrote.
years.xp: A tribute night followed, with Salisbury on drums and [[Beady Eye|a0e10984-0eca-4920-a171-5fd7a62ee069]], The Vaccines and [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]] on the bill. The money went to The Brain Tumour Charity, which set up the Jon Brookes Fund; the band became patrons.

years.h: Modern Nature, with three drummers sitting in
years.p: Salisbury, New Order's [[Stephen Morris|b3036249-8b39-4d02-a312-d31a63497bbc]] and Factory Floor's Gabriel Gurnsey share Brookes's stool. The first album on BMG.

years.h: Paul Weller, Johnny Marr and Kurt Wagner on Different Days
years.p: The thirteenth studio album. Every one of the band's albums so far has made the UK Top 40.

eras.title: Tim's Twitter Listening Party
eras.text: When lockdown shut the venues, Burgess started playing albums on Twitter with the artists in the replies. He began with his own band's debut. By the end of 2020 there had been 617.

years.h: Burgess starts the listening parties with Some Friendly
years.p: Fans play the record at the same time while the musicians tweet along. 617 albums get the treatment in 2020 alone.

years.h: Back on a festival stage in Belgium
years.p: They play Crammerock in Stekene. The Covid-delayed box set A Head Full of Ideas follows on October 15, and the UK tour opens at the Limelight, Belfast, on November 22.

years.h: We Are Love, number fourteen
years.p: Burgess announced the return on X on July 12; the title track was out two days later.
